                    ### Question
                    One patient is diagnosed with a 4 cm lung cancer without pleural contact in the right upper lobe. The extension study reveals the presence of metastasis in right parahilar nodes, without evidence of distant metastasis. The staging of the tumor will be:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Stage I.
opb. Stage IIA.
opc. Stage IIB.
opd. Stage IIIA.
ope. Stage IIIB.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient has a 4 cm lung cancer located in the right upper lobe, with metastasis to the right parahilar lymph nodes and no evidence of distant metastasis. According to the American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) staging system, lung cancer staging considers tumor size, location, and lymph node involvement. The presence of regional lymph node metastasis (N1 or N2) in conjunction with a tumor size of 4 cm classifies the cancer as Stage IIIA. Therefore, the correct staging for this patient is Stage IIIA, as supported by the reasoning chains that consistently point to this classification based on the presence of regional lymph node involvement without distant spread.
